## Analysis

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

## Data Gathering, Analysis and QA

```{r}
source(here::here("data-raw", "build_daily_forcing.R"))
source(here::here("data-raw", "arrival_sanity_checks.R"))
source(here::here("data-raw", "fetch_dahiti.R"))

#Remasking ERA5 Cells to polygon
source(here::here("data-raw", "remask_forcing_to_reservoir.R"))

#NASA Power data download
source(here::here("data-raw", "fetch_nasa_power.R"))

```

```{r}
daily <- to_daily(hourly, mean_vars = c("d2m","sp","u10","v10","lmlt","lmld","skt"), sum_vars = c("ssrd","strd","str","tp","e","pev"), minmax_vars = "t2m")

forcing <- standardise_forcing(daily, source = "era5_land", wind = "from_uv")
out <- Eopen_Penman(forcing, lat_deg = 37.5, elev_m = 542)
```

## Appendix: computational environment {#sec-environment .appendix}

```{=html}
<!--
Paste this at the end of the main .qmd, after all analysis chunks.

It records three things, in decreasing order of how often they turn out
to matter:

  1. Which commit and which data produced this output
  2. Whether renv was actually honoured at render time
  3. Package and R versions

sessionInfo() alone covers only (3). With renv in place that is the
least informative of the three, because renv.lock already documents the
intended state. What sessionInfo() adds is evidence of the ACTUAL state,
which is worth having precisely when it disagrees with the lockfile.

NOTE: this appendix used to be a single R chunk holding all four labelled
sections below. That produced a "duplicate map key: label" YAML error
(renv's dependency scanner reads all `#|` lines in one chunk as one
options block) and silently made renv skip this file when enumerating
dependencies. Fixed by giving each labelled section its own chunk.
-->
```

```{r}
#| label: env-provenance
#| echo: false
#| comment: ""

# --- render metadata -------------------------------------------------
cat("Rendered:      ", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Working dir:   ", here::here(), "\n", sep = "")

# --- git state -------------------------------------------------------
# A commit SHA is misleading on its own: if the working tree is dirty,
# the recorded commit did not produce this output. Report both.
git <- tryCatch({
  sha   <- system2("git", c("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"),
                   stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)
  dirty <- length(system2("git", c("status", "--porcelain"),
                          stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)) > 0
  list(sha = sha, dirty = dirty)
}, error = function(e) NULL, warning = function(w) NULL)

if (is.null(git) || !length(git$sha)) {
  cat("Git commit:    unavailable (not a repo, or git not on PATH)\n")
} else {
  cat("Git commit:    ", git$sha,
      if (git$dirty) "  [UNCOMMITTED CHANGES PRESENT]" else "  (clean tree)",
      "\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: env-data-provenance
#| echo: false
#| comment: ""

# --- input data fingerprints -----------------------------------------
# The single most useful line in this appendix. Package versions rarely
# change a result; a silently re-downloaded or re-processed input file
# routinely does. Checksums make that visible.
#
# Point this at the processed inputs the analysis actually reads, not at
# the raw ERA5-Land NetCDFs (too large, and not what the chain consumes).

data_files <- c(
  here::here("data", "forcing_era5land_daily.rds"),
  here::here("data", "forcing_nasapower_daily.rds"),
  here::here("data", "area_dahiti.rds"),
  here::here("data", "area_jrc.rds"),
  here::here("data", "lst_modis.rds")
)

present <- data_files[file.exists(data_files)]

if (!length(present)) {
  cat("No processed input files found at the expected paths.\n")
} else {
  info <- data.frame(
    file     = basename(present),
    size_MB  = round(file.size(present) / 1024^2, 2),
    modified = format(file.mtime(present), "%Y-%m-%d"),
    md5      = substr(unname(tools::md5sum(present)), 1, 12),
    row.names = NULL
  )
  print(info, right = FALSE)
}

absent <- setdiff(data_files, present)
if (length(absent))
  cat("\nExpected but not found: ",
      paste(basename(absent), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: env-renv
#| echo: false
#| comment: ""

# --- was renv actually honoured? -------------------------------------
if (requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) {
  st <- tryCatch(renv::status(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(st)) {
    cat("renv installed but no project state could be read.\n")
  } else if (isTRUE(st$synchronized)) {
    cat("renv: library synchronised with renv.lock\n")
  } else {
    cat("renv: LIBRARY OUT OF SYNC WITH renv.lock.\n",
        "      Run renv::status() interactively before trusting these results.\n",
        sep = "")
  }
} else {
  cat("renv not installed — package versions below are not reproducible.\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: env-session
#| echo: false
#| comment: ""

# sessioninfo::session_info() is preferred over base sessionInfo(): it
# reports the SOURCE of each package (CRAN, Bioconductor, GitHub SHA),
# which base R omits and which matters if anything came from GitHub.
if (requireNamespace("sessioninfo", quietly = TRUE)) {
  sessioninfo::session_info(to_file = FALSE)
} else {
  sessionInfo()
}
```

```{=html}
<!--
NOTE ON PLACEMENT AND CACHING

sessionInfo() reports packages attached AT THIS POINT in the render. Two
ways that becomes a lie:

  - Chunk caching (`cache: true`). Cached chunks do not re-attach their
    packages, so a package used by a cached analysis chunk may be absent
    from this listing. If you cache anything, say so in Methods.

  - Rendering the document in pieces during development. The appendix
    reflects the session that rendered it, not the session that produced
    each figure. Before submission, render once end-to-end from a clean
    session (`renv::restore()`, then Quarto render) and use THAT output.

For the code availability statement, cite the commit SHA reported above,
and tag it in the repo so the reference is stable:

    git tag -a submission-v1 -m "State at journal submission"
    git push origin submission-v1
-->
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
